lessons.goal: 以路線方向與現場標示核對乘車資訊。

questions.evidence: A city changes the name of a bus stop near Mara's home from Library Corner to Civic Center. The stop itself remains in the same place. Mara sees the new name on a digital map and assumes the bus now follows a different road.
questions.prompt: What actually changes at the stop?

questions.evidence: At the stop, a notice explains that only the name has changed. The route number and travel direction are unchanged. However, the stop across the road serves the opposite direction, so choosing by the shared place name alone can still lead to the wrong bus.
questions.prompt: What does the stop across the road serve?

questions.evidence: Mara checks the route number, direction arrow, and next two stops before boarding. She tells her grandfather about the new name and marks the familiar library building on a small map. He recognizes the landmark even though the printed stop name is unfamiliar.
questions.explanation: 熟悉地標幫助銜接陌生新名稱。
options: It proves the library has moved.
It connects the new name with a place he knows.
questions.prompt: Why include the familiar library landmark for her grandfather?

questions.evidence: Later, Mara updates a meeting message without saying the stop moved. She writes new name, same location and includes the direction toward the station. The short clarification preserves what people already know while pointing out exactly what they need to notice.
questions.explanation: 簡短說明釐清名稱改、地點不變。
options: Information making a confusing point clear.

questions.evidence: Mara checks the route number, direction arrow, and next two stops before boarding. She tells her grandfather about the new name and marks the familiar library building on a small map. He recognizes the landmark even though the printed stop name is unfamiliar.
questions.explanation: 核對路線與方向、後續站點才可確認。
options: Only the color of the map.
Route number, direction arrow, and next stops.
questions.prompt: Which checks reduce the chance of boarding the wrong direction?

lessons.story:
A city changes the name of a bus stop near Mara's home from Library Corner to Civic Center. The stop itself remains in the same place. Mara sees the new name on a digital map and assumes the bus now follows a different road.

At the stop, a notice explains that only the name has changed. The route number and travel direction are unchanged. However, the stop across the road serves the opposite direction, so choosing by the shared place name alone can still lead to the wrong bus.

Mara checks the route number, direction arrow, and next two stops before boarding. She tells her grandfather about the new name and marks the familiar library building on a small map. He recognizes the landmark even though the printed stop name is unfamiliar.

Later, Mara updates a meeting message without saying the stop moved. She writes new name, same location and includes the direction toward the station. The short clarification preserves what people already know while pointing out exactly what they need to notice.
lessons.title: The Bus Stop Name Has Moved
